text:
Maria: Heads-up — saw a perf regression in the kernel chooser when sequences move from ~2k to ~4k on mixed GQA/MQA runs. KV-cache hit rate drops and we get more expensive paged-attn path picks.
Aj: ugh. which model + hardware?
Maria: Llama-2-70B on A100-80GB, batch=1 steady-state, but spike happens on longer sequences after warmup when KV fragmentation increases.
Sylvie: do you have a flamegraph or perf counters?
Maria: quick traces attached (pasted):
```
time   kernel_pick   seqlen   kv_hits   latency_ms
12:23  hybrid_v2      2048     0.97      42
12:38  hybrid_v2      4096     0.64      87  <-- jump
12:39  paged_attn_b2  4096     0.60      82
```
Deepak: looks like our hysteresis threshold is 3072, so when an input crosses, the picker flips immediately. KV layout change + prefetch not keeping up.
Casey: can we clamp picks based on observed KV hit ratio, not just seqlen? e.g., require >0.8 hit for hybrid_v2 to stay.
Ben: +1. We already collect kv_hit_rate metric per-request. Might be cheap to add a short-term EWMA and gate.
Maria: I ran microbench after toggling gate: EWMA over last 8 requests, threshold 0.75 — latency stabilized, fewer expensive paged-attn switches.
Aj: what's the failure mode? oscillation or one-way regression?
Maria: mostly oscillation across 3-5 requests as some requests clear cache (longer tails), so picker flips back-and-forth causing extra kernel load and memory churn.
Sylvie: idea: introduce prefetch hysteresis where prefetch is kept enabled for N tokens after switch unless hit_rate drops below X. That prevents immediate backflip.
Deepak: also worth looking at blocksize alignment — our paged-attn_b2 uses block=256; for 4096 seqlen with MQA we might get more fragmentation. Try block=512 in probe.
Casey: can you run the probe with these two knobs? Gate by EWMA + blocksize 512. Use the perf harness: `./run_probe --model llama-2-70b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --runs 200 --block 512 --ewma_window 8 --ewma_thresh 0.75`
Maria: running now, will post microbench numbers shortly.
(ops-bot): perf-probe job 2471234567 started on infra-12
Maria: results pasted:
```
config: block=256, ewma=false -> p95=89ms, kv_hit=0.62, kernel_switches=18
config: block=512, ewma=true  -> p95=68ms, kv_hit=0.81, kernel_switches=3
```
Ben: huge win. lower p95 and fewer switches. Block 512 reduces fragmentation and EWMA prevents flip-flop.
Aj: any memory/reg cost for block=512?
Maria: minor bump in peak GPU memory (~3%) but within headroom on A100-80. On 40GB cards it might be tighter.
Sylvie: we should add a hardware-aware policy: prefer block=512 for >32GB cards and block=256 for smaller ones, combined with EWMA gate. Add to kernel_autotune table.
Deepak: agree. I'll sketch migration plan: 1) add EWMA metric to picker, 2) add blocksize heuristics by device mem, 3) safe rollout with canary on dedicated pool.
Casey: also record a new metric: kernel_switch_rate per-minute so SRE/alerts catch regressions early.
Maria: filed perf ticket INF-1124 with logs and microbench output, put canary config in /configs/kernel-autotune/2471234567-canary.json.
Ben: nice. @ops-bot can you schedule a canary rollout for tomorrow 09:00 UTC to 10:00?
(ops-bot): scheduled canary rollout window 2026-03-19T09:00:00Z - 2026-03-19T10:00:00Z for config kernel-autotune/canary-2471234567
Aj: after canary, let's run 24h trace to ensure no slow drift.
Maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
